name: Ceramic armour plate
description: A curved ceramic plate in a black fabric cover, made to slide into a plate carrier.
notes: 250 by 300 mm, 12 mm thick, curved across its width, with shooter's cuts at the top corners and a white label on the cover. The reference's 362 g is far below a real plate's 2 kg or so; the reference mass is kept. Fitting it into a carrier or vest has no content field yet. The size is a placeholder.

name: Steel chain
description: A heavy length of steel chain with round links.
notes: About 2.4 m of 8 mm stock with 40 mm round links, laid flat in four runs joined at the turns; that much steel weighs the reference's 3.6 kg. CHECK VOLUME (x4.8): the box counts the air between the runs and inside the links; the steel alone is about the reference's 1 L. tying is a new quality name for the reference's ROPE quality. Swinging it as a weapon has no melee block in this draft.

name: Gold chalice
description: A gold cup on a knopped stem and a wide foot.
notes: 120 mm tall with an 80 mm cup. Its worth as a valuable has no content field yet.

name: Chamomile flowers
description: A handful of small white daisy-like flowers with yellow centres, picked for tea.
notes: Six heads 20 mm across on short stems, lying face up. cloth-white draws the petals, plastic-yellow the centres and plant-dried the stems. Brewing it into tea or using it as a remedy needs recipes.

name: Circular saw blade
description: An 8 inch steel saw blade with 24 hooked teeth.
notes: 204 mm across, a 2 mm plate with a 16 mm arbor hole inside a blued collar. Making a saw from it, or throwing it, needs recipes and a thrown-weapon block.

name: Lump of clay
description: A soft lump of fresh clay, ready to be shaped or fired.
notes: About 90 by 70 mm and 45 mm high. clay-terracotta draws it; a damp unfired clay finish would tell it apart from the fired pot. Shaping and firing need recipes.

name: Clay flower pot
description: A terracotta pot with a rolled rim, for growing plants.
notes: 155 mm tall and 176 mm across the rim. Planting in it has no content field yet.

name: Alarm clock
description: A red wind-up alarm clock with two bells on top, stopped at ten past ten.
notes: 110 mm across and 150 mm tall with bells, hammer, winding key and two feet. CHECK VOLUME (x4.6): the reference's 250 ml is small for a clock of its 725 g; the box also counts the air round the bells and feet. Taking it apart for clockworks needs a disassembly block.

name: Clockworks
description: A few small brass gears, a steel pinion and a balance wheel.
notes: About 70 mm across: three brass gears meshing on their arbors, a pinion on the largest, and a loose balance wheel. Use in crafting needs recipes.

name: Sack of concrete mix
description: A small paper sack of dry cement, sand and gravel, mixed and ready to wet.
notes: Loose powder, drawn in the small paper sack a player would carry, 80 by 50 mm and 90 mm tall with its top rolled down, a printed band and a little spilled grey mix beside it. Mixing with water and pouring need recipes.

name: Condensing unit
description: A refrigeration compressor and fan on a steel base, with a finned copper condenser coil.
notes: 400 by 260 mm and about 300 mm tall: a domed compressor, a four-blade fan in its shroud and a finned coil with copper passes, joined by two copper lines. CHECK VOLUME (x15.6): the reference's 2 L cannot hold a 20 kg compressor, fan and coil; the drawn size is kept and the box also counts the air round the parts. Building a fridge or freezer from it needs recipes. The size is a placeholder.

name: Cottonwood fluff
description: A loose white tuft of cottonwood seed fluff, too short and weak to spin.
notes: About 80 mm across: five overlapping white puffs with a small brown seed showing. Use as tinder or stuffing needs recipes.

name: Crude heating element
description: A coil of steel wire wound by hand, with a terminal loop at each end. It burns out quickly.
notes: 4 mm wire in 24 open turns on a 34 mm coil 200 mm long, with straight leads ending in loops, 300 mm overall; that much wire weighs about the reference's 226 g. Fitting it to a heater or stove needs recipes, and its faster wear has no content field yet.

name: Delay fuze
description: A small clockwork fuze with a striker lever and a safety pin. It fires a few seconds after the pin is pulled.
notes: 38 mm long and 14 mm across: a threaded steel nose, an olive plastic body, a lever along the top and a pin with a pull ring. CHECK VOLUME (x4.1): the reference's 5 ml is its minimum; the box counts the ring standing off the side. Fitting it to an explosive needs recipes.

name: Diamond
description: A cut diamond, about one carat.
notes: A 6.5 mm round brilliant would be a few voxels at the 2 mm grain, so the model, like the pill packages, is what a player would pick up: the stone lying on the opened paper loose stones are sold in, 70 by 40 mm with a blue liner. The mass is the stone's 0.2 g. The box is about 3.8 times the reference volume because it is the paper; the reference 6 ml is its minimum. gem-clear draws the stone; the tiles draw it opaque, but it stays see-through in the game. Setting it in jewellery needs recipes.
